hero.supportingStatement: Snap-8 (Acetyl Octapeptide-3) is a synthetic octapeptide modeled on a short sequence from SNAP-25, a protein involved in the cellular SNARE fusion complex. Veracue presents this page as a molecular identity and research-documentation reference for laboratory work — not as a skincare, cosmetic or consumer recommendation.
hero.shortDescription: Snap-8 is a synthetic octapeptide (Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-Ala-Asp-NH2) modeled on a short sequence from SNAP-25, listed by many suppliers as Acetyl Octapeptide-3. Veracue presents it as a research material for laboratory work. Most published material discusses Snap-8 within cosmetic-formulation research rather than as an isolated, independently tested compound, and no independently published human clinical trial of Snap-8 alone was identified, so this material does not establish cosmetic efficacy, treatment effect or safety in people.

aeo.question: What is Snap-8 peptide?
aeo.answer: Snap-8 peptide is a synthetic octapeptide (Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-Ala-Asp-NH2) modeled on a short sequence from SNAP-25, a protein that forms part of the SNARE membrane-fusion complex. Snap-8 is not a naturally occurring SNAP-25 fragment — it is a laboratory-synthesized peptide corresponding to part of that sequence, studied in relation to the SNARE mechanism. Most published material involves cosmetic formulation or cell-based research rather than the isolated peptide in controlled human studies. Veracue presents Snap-8 strictly for laboratory research use, not for human or veterinary administration.

molecularIdentity.heading: Molecular Identity
molecularIdentity.body: Snap-8 is a short synthetic peptide — eight amino acids in a single chain, built in a lab rather than isolated from a natural source. Its full sequence, written in standard three-letter amino-acid code, is Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-Ala-Asp-NH2. Reading that left to right: two glutamic acid residues, a methionine, a glutamine, two arginines, an alanine, and an aspartic acid, capped at both ends. The 'Ac-' at the front means the N-terminus carries an acetyl group instead of a free amine, and the '-NH2' at the end means the C-terminus is amidated rather than left as a free carboxylic acid. Both modifications are common in synthetic peptide chemistry — they tend to improve a peptide's stability against enzymes that would otherwise chew through it from either end. PubChem currently associates CAS 868844-74-0 with Acetyl Octapeptide-3 (PubChem CID 76283482) and records the sequence, molecular formula (C41H70N16O16S) and molecular weight (1075.2 g/mol) shown here; this CAS-linked record is used as the reference identity for this page. Public chemical databases contain more than one deposited record associated with Acetyl Octapeptide-3 terminology, with occasional differences in the structure or formula shown. For the identity presented here, the CAS-linked PubChem record matching CAS 868844-74-0 is used because its sequence and molecular formula correspond to the conventional Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-Ala-Asp-NH2 structure. Because chemical databases can contain deposited records with inconsistent naming or structure representations, the identity of a specific research lot should still be confirmed using that lot's own analytical documentation rather than a database record or a name printed on a vial. Reference identity comes from authoritative chemical records; lot identity comes from lot-specific analytical documentation — those are two different things, and this page only speaks to the first.

researchContext.heading: SNAP-25 and the Proposed Mechanism
researchContext.body: SNAP-25 (synaptosomal-associated protein of 25 kDa) is a well-characterized full-length protein that, together with syntaxin-1 and VAMP/synaptobrevin, forms the core SNARE complex responsible for vesicle docking and membrane fusion in cells — the process underlying regulated exocytosis, including neurotransmitter release at synapses. Snap-8 is a synthetic peptide corresponding to a short stretch of SNAP-25's sequence, on the premise that this free-standing peptide might occupy space within the SNARE assembly process and interfere with its normal formation. It is important to be precise about what that means: Snap-8 does not 'block SNAP-25' in the sense of inhibiting or degrading the protein directly, and it is not itself a naturally occurring fragment isolated from SNAP-25 — it is a laboratory-made peptide designed to correspond to part of that sequence. The proposed interaction is structural and competitive — a hypothesis about a short synthetic peptide interfering with complex assembly — rather than an established enzymatic or pharmacological mechanism. The bulk of the documentation behind this design rationale originates from cosmetic-ingredient development and patent literature rather than an extensive, independent body of peer-reviewed mechanistic study. Researchers evaluating Snap-8 should treat the SNARE-interference concept as the working hypothesis the material was designed around, not as a demonstrated mechanism of action in every experimental system.

evidenceSummary.heading: Evidence Hierarchy

categories.summary: Snap-8's sequence, mass and general chemical properties are documented across independent chemical-supplier and reference sources. This establishes what the molecule is, not what it does biologically.

Some cell-based work referencing SNARE-complex peptides exists in the literature, but sources reviewed did not consistently isolate Snap-8 alone, distinct from the broader class of SNAP-25-derived research peptides.
I did not identify a substantial, independently published body of ex vivo tissue-based research isolating Snap-8 specifically in the sources reviewed.
I did not identify a substantial, independently published body of animal-model research isolating Snap-8 specifically in the sources reviewed.

I did not identify an independently published, controlled human clinical trial testing Snap-8 as a single isolated compound in the sources reviewed. Human-facing efficacy figures circulating online generally trace to supplier or brand marketing material rather than peer-reviewed publication.

A small number of PubMed-indexed sources reference acetyl octapeptide-3, typically as one of several active ingredients within a multi-component topical formulation (such as a combination patch or cream) rather than as an isolated, independently tested peptide. A formulation result of this kind describes the finished product, not the purified compound on its own.

evidenceSummary.keyPrinciple: A formulation study is not automatically evidence that the purified research peptide produces the same effect. Molecular reference data, published research, experimental models, and Veracue's own product documentation are four separate things and should not be collapsed into a single claim.

problemSolutions.problem: How do I confirm that a material is actually Snap-8?
problemSolutions.solution: Snap-8 is sold under a small number of overlapping names — Acetyl Octapeptide-3 and SNAP-8 both appear on supplier listings for the same general compound, and naming conventions vary further across databases and suppliers beyond that. A product label or trade name alone doesn't establish identity. Confirmation should rest on the documented sequence (Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-Ala-Asp-NH2), the CAS number 868844-74-0, and the molecular formula C41H70N16O16S from the CAS-linked PubChem record, cross-checked against a specific lot's own mass spectrometry and HPLC results rather than the name printed on the vial.

problemSolutions.problem: What exactly is the relationship between Snap-8 and SNAP-25?
problemSolutions.solution: SNAP-25 is the full-length, well-studied protein that forms part of the SNARE complex governing vesicle fusion in cells. Snap-8 is a short synthetic peptide modeled on a sequence near SNAP-25's N-terminal region — it is not a naturally occurring fragment isolated from SNAP-25 itself. It does not replace SNAP-25 and does not cleave it enzymatically. The design premise is that this synthetic peptide might compete for a position within the SNARE assembly process — a structural hypothesis, not a demonstrated therapeutic mechanism.

problemSolutions.problem: Is Snap-8 the same thing as Argireline or acetyl hexapeptide-8?
problemSolutions.solution: Argireline is a related, shorter six-residue peptide, identified in chemical records under more than one name — Acetyl Hexapeptide-3 and Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 both appear across databases for the same general peptide (Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-NH2). Naming conventions for this class of peptide vary across sources; the numbering is not settled the same way everywhere. What is consistent is that Snap-8 extends that sequence by two additional residues (alanine and aspartic acid), producing a distinct 8-residue compound with its own molecular formula, weight and CAS registration. Argireline and Snap-8 share a design lineage but are different peptides and should not be treated as interchangeable.

problemSolutions.problem: How should I interpret the Snap-8 sequence and chemical form?
problemSolutions.solution: The sequence Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-Ala-Asp-NH2 describes eight residues with a capped N-terminus (acetylation) and a capped C-terminus (amidation) — modifications commonly used in synthetic peptide chemistry to slow enzymatic degradation from either end. Supplier documentation frequently lists the compound as an acetate salt, but the specific salt form and counterion of any individual research lot should be confirmed against that lot's own analytical paperwork rather than assumed from general chemical listings.

problemSolutions.problem: What does the published mechanism research actually show?
problemSolutions.solution: SNAP-25 and the broader SNARE complex are well characterized in neuroscience and cell biology generally. What is less established is an extensive, independent body of mechanistic research testing Snap-8 itself against that system. Most of the mechanistic rationale for Snap-8 traces back to cosmetic-ingredient development and patent-style documentation rather than a wide base of independently replicated biochemical studies isolating the peptide.

problemSolutions.problem: How should I interpret cosmetic or topical Snap-8 studies?
problemSolutions.solution: Cosmetic or formulation studies test a finished product — a cream, serum or patch containing Snap-8 alongside other active ingredients at defined concentrations — applied to skin. A result from that kind of study reflects the whole formulation, not Snap-8's individual, isolated contribution, and it says nothing about how a purified research-grade peptide behaves outside that formulated, topical context.

problemSolutions.problem: What do "Snap-8 benefits" searches actually mean in research terms?
problemSolutions.solution: Search interest in 'Snap-8 benefits' generally reflects consumer cosmetic marketing language rather than a specific experimental finding. In research terms, the underlying material has been discussed mainly in the context of SNARE-complex-related peptide design and cosmetic formulation development. Veracue's Snap-8 material is intended for laboratory study of that research context, not as a substantiation of any consumer benefit claim.

problemSolutions.problem: What does Snap-8 research say about human evidence?
problemSolutions.solution: The sources reviewed did not surface an independently published, controlled human clinical trial testing Snap-8 as a single isolated compound. Where human-facing figures do appear online, they generally originate from manufacturer or brand marketing materials rather than peer-reviewed publication, and cannot be treated as equivalent to independently verified clinical evidence.

problemSolutions.problem: How should I compare Snap-8 with GHK-Cu?
problemSolutions.solution: Snap-8 and GHK-Cu are structurally and mechanistically unrelated compounds that happen to be discussed in similar consumer-facing contexts. Snap-8 is a synthetic 8-residue peptide built around a proposed SNARE-complex interaction; GHK-Cu is the naturally occurring copper(II) complex of the tripeptide Gly-His-Lys, studied in a different research literature centered on copper-peptide signaling. Neither is a substitute for the other, and neither should be treated as more or less 'valid' than the other — see the comparison table for a side-by-side of documented attributes.

problemSolutions.problem: What should I verify on a Snap-8 COA?
problemSolutions.solution: A lot-specific COA may include the material name and lot/batch identifier, sequence or identity confirmation, the analytical method used, HPLC-reported purity (often with a chromatogram), mass spectrometry identity data, the testing date, the testing laboratory, and chemical form or counterion information where relevant. No Snap-8-specific COA is currently published in Veracue's archive; this list describes what lot documentation may include in general, not a result Veracue has published for this compound.

problemSolutions.problem: How should I interpret Snap-8 mass-spectrometry results?
problemSolutions.solution: Molecular weight and the mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) reported by a mass spectrometer are not the same number — peptides commonly ionize into multiple charge states, and salts or adducts can shift the observed ion mass relative to the peptide's neutral molecular weight. Mass spectrometry is primarily used to confirm identity (does the observed mass match the theoretical sequence mass, within an expected tolerance), while chromatography (HPLC) is what's typically used to assess purity and composition. No specific expected peak pattern for Snap-8 is asserted here beyond this general interpretive framework.

problemSolutions.problem: What can a Veracue Snap-8 product page establish versus lot-specific documentation?
problemSolutions.solution: This page can establish general molecular reference information (sequence, formula, weight, CAS) and summarize published research context and its limitations. It cannot establish the purity, identity or composition of any individual lot of material — that requires lot-specific analytical documentation (COA) tied to the exact batch a researcher receives. Treat this page as background and orientation, and treat a lot's own COA as the operative record for that lot.

massSpecGuide.heading: Reading Snap-8 Mass Spectrometry Data
massSpecGuide.body: Molecular weight is not the same figure as the mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) reported on a mass spectrum. Peptides frequently ionize into more than one charge state during electrospray ionization, and the presence of salts or adducts can shift the observed ion mass relative to a peptide's calculated neutral molecular weight. Mass spectrometry is primarily used to confirm identity — checking that an observed mass matches the sequence's theoretical mass within an expected tolerance — while chromatographic methods like HPLC are typically what establish purity and composition. This page does not assert a specific expected dominant peak for Snap-8, since that figure depends on the exact instrument, ionization method and chemical form used for a given lot.

faq.question: What is Snap-8 peptide?
faq.answer: Snap-8 is a synthetic octapeptide (Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-Ala-Asp-NH2) modeled on a short sequence from SNAP-25, a protein involved in the SNARE membrane-fusion complex. It is supplied by Veracue for laboratory research only.

faq.question: What is the Snap-8 sequence?
faq.answer: Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-Ala-Asp-NH2 — eight amino acid residues with an acetylated N-terminus and an amidated C-terminus.

faq.question: Is Snap-8 the same as Argireline?
faq.answer: No. Argireline is a related, shorter six-residue peptide — identified in chemical records as both Acetyl Hexapeptide-3 and Acetyl Hexapeptide-8, depending on the source. Snap-8 extends that sequence with two additional residues, forming a distinct 8-residue compound with its own molecular formula, weight and CAS number.

faq.question: Is Snap-8 related to SNAP-25?
faq.answer: Yes, by design. Snap-8 is a synthetic peptide corresponding to a short sequence from SNAP-25, developed around the hypothesis that this peptide interacts with the SNARE assembly process. It is not SNAP-25 itself, not a naturally occurring fragment isolated from it, and does not enzymatically cleave or replace it.

faq.question: What does Snap-8 research investigate?
faq.answer: Published material on Snap-8 mostly concerns its proposed role in SNARE-complex-related peptide design and its use as an ingredient in cosmetic formulation research, rather than an extensive independent mechanistic literature.

faq.question: Does Snap-8 have human research?
faq.answer: The sources reviewed did not identify an independently published, controlled human clinical trial testing Snap-8 as a single isolated compound.

faq.question: What do Snap-8 "benefits" refer to in research literature?
faq.answer: Consumer-facing 'benefits' language generally traces to cosmetic marketing rather than isolated, peer-reviewed findings. In research terms, the material is discussed mainly within SNARE-related peptide design and formulation development.

faq.question: How is Snap-8 different from GHK-Cu?
faq.answer: They are unrelated compounds. Snap-8 is a synthetic 8-residue peptide built around a proposed SNARE-complex interaction; GHK-Cu is a naturally occurring copper-binding tripeptide studied in a separate research context. See the comparison table for details.

faq.question: What is the molecular weight of Snap-8?
faq.answer: 1075.2 g/mol, with a molecular formula of C41H70N16O16S, per the PubChem record (CID 76283482) linked to CAS 868844-74-0.

faq.question: What should a Snap-8 COA show?
faq.answer: A COA may include the lot identifier, sequence/identity confirmation, HPLC purity data, mass spectrometry identity results, testing date, testing laboratory, and chemical form. No Snap-8-specific COA is currently published by Veracue.

faq.question: How should Snap-8 mass spectrometry be interpreted?
faq.answer: By comparing the observed mass-to-charge ratio, accounting for charge state and possible adducts, against the peptide's theoretical molecular weight — rather than expecting a single fixed peak value.

faq.question: Is Veracue Snap-8 intended for human use?
faq.answer: No. Veracue presents Snap-8 strictly for laboratory research use. It is not intended for human or veterinary use, diagnosis, treatment, prevention or mitigation of disease.
